facts: **Latitude** measures degrees north or south from the **Equator** ($0^{\circ}$), ranging from $90^{\circ}\text{S}$ to $90^{\circ}\text{N}$.
**Longitude** measures degrees east or west from the **Prime Meridian** ($0^{\circ}$), ranging from $180^{\circ}\text{W}$ to $180^{\circ}\text{E}$.
Coordinates are written as $(\text{latitude}, \text{longitude})$, such as $(30^{\circ}\text{N}, 45^{\circ}\text{E})$.
The **Equator** has latitude $0^{\circ}$, and the **Prime Meridian** has longitude $0^{\circ}$.
In digital coordinates, negative values represent south latitudes or west longitudes, such as $-33.8^{\circ} = 33.8^{\circ}\text{S}$.

foundation.question_text:

Do these two cities share the same parallel of latitude or the same meridian of longitude?
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Latitude of } X = 35^{\circ}\text{S}$
$\text{Latitude of } Y = 35^{\circ}\text{S}$
$\text{Longitude of } X = 140^{\circ}\text{E}$
$\text{Longitude of } Y = 175^{\circ}\text{E}$
Both cities have a latitude of $35^{\circ}\text{S}$, so they share the same parallel of latitude.

development.question_text:
Town $A$ is at $(15^{\circ}\text{N}, 120^{\circ}\text{E})$ and Town $B$ is at $(15^{\circ}\text{S}, 120^{\circ}\text{E})$.
State which feature of their coordinates is identical and which feature is opposite.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Longitude of } A = 120^{\circ}\text{E}$
$\text{Longitude of } B = 120^{\circ}\text{E}$
Both towns lie on the same meridian of longitude ($120^{\circ}\text{E}$).
$\text{Latitude of } A = 15^{\circ}\text{N}$
$\text{Latitude of } B = 15^{\circ}\text{S}$
Their latitudes have the same angle magnitude ($15^{\circ}$) but lie in opposite hemispheres (North vs South).

development.question_text:
A globe shows four locations: $W(45^{\circ}\text{N}, 10^{\circ}\text{E})$, $X(45^{\circ}\text{S}, 10^{\circ}\text{W})$, $Y(10^{\circ}\text{N}, 45^{\circ}\text{E})$, and $Z(45^{\circ}\text{N}, 10^{\circ}\text{W})$.
Which point is located in the Northern and Western hemispheres?
development.solution_text:
Northern hemisphere means latitude is $^{\circ}\text{N}$.
Western hemisphere means longitude is $^{\circ}\text{W}$.
Checking the points:
$W = (45^{\circ}\text{N}, 10^{\circ}\text{E}) \to$ North, East
$X = (45^{\circ}\text{S}, 10^{\circ}\text{W}) \to$ South, West
$Y = (10^{\circ}\text{N}, 45^{\circ}\text{E}) \to$ North, East
$Z = (45^{\circ}\text{N}, 10^{\circ}\text{W}) \to$ North, West
Point $Z$ is in the Northern and Western hemispheres.

development.question_text: Identify which of the following represents a valid position on Earth: $(105^{\circ}\text{N}, 45^{\circ}\text{E})$, $(45^{\circ}\text{N}, 195^{\circ}\text{E})$, $(75^{\circ}\text{S}, 150^{\circ}\text{W})$, or $(30^{\circ}\text{E}, 60^{\circ}\text{N})$.
development.solution_text:
Latitude must be between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}\text{N/S}$, and longitude between $0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}\text{E/W}$, written as $(\text{lat}, \text{long})$.
- $105^{\circ}\text{N}$ exceeds the maximum latitude of $90^{\circ}$.
- $195^{\circ}\text{E}$ exceeds the maximum longitude of $180^{\circ}$.
- $(30^{\circ}\text{E}, 60^{\circ}\text{N})$ lists longitude first, violating the coordinate convention.
- $(75^{\circ}\text{S}, 150^{\circ}\text{W})$ has valid latitude ($75^{\circ} \le 90^{\circ}$) and longitude ($150^{\circ} \le 180^{\circ}$) in correct order.
$(75^{\circ}\text{S}, 150^{\circ}\text{W})$ is the only valid position.

mastery.question_text:
A GPS device outputs decimal coordinates as $(-33.9, 151.2)$, where negative values denote southern latitudes and western longitudes.
Convert these coordinates into standard degree-hemisphere notation.

A digital map query returns coordinates for three research stations: Station $1$ at $(-42.8, -65.3)$, Station $2$ at $(42.8, -65.3)$, and Station $3$ at $(-42.8, 65.3)$.
Express the coordinates of Station $1$ in standard $(\text{lat}, \text{long})$ notation and identify which hemisphere pair it belongs to.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Latitude} = -42.8 \implies 42.8^{\circ}\text{S}$
$\text{Longitude} = -65.3 \implies 65.3^{\circ}\text{W}$
$\text{Coordinates} = (42.8^{\circ}\text{S}, 65.3^{\circ}\text{W})$
Station $1$ is located in the Southern and Western hemispheres.

mastery.question_text: Convert the standard coordinates $(18.5^{\circ}\text{N}, 72.3^{\circ}\text{W})$ into signed decimal coordinates as used in digital search queries.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{North latitude is positive} \implies +18.5$
$\text{West longitude is negative} \implies -72.3$
$\text{Signed coordinates} = (18.5, -72.3)$
